title: The visiting star, a dressing-room razor fight and the anthems
summary: A star and a dancer called Flash fought in the dressing room; when the star demanded God Bless America before the British anthem, Butler calmed disorderly soldiers.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So, I joined their local and we was wailing so much up there and you see, it's very, very cold As you know. Andif you don't wear rubbers, you just gone -- you die. Now, you can go up there and be cute if you want to but -- and so we're playing and at that time the war's on and a certain big star, the name is not going to be there so don't ask about the name.
So, she come up there and another dancer she was named Flash, and it seems they got to arguing in the dressing room and
somebody called somebody a black bitch.
And somebody asked them -- a razor blade, wanted to cut the other one's face or something and the other one was off there looking for, I think, a hunting knife and so I saw that.

Then, that was all right, they kind of settled that but everybody was ill at ease and there was a man his name was -- great singer -- I called him Preacher. And the man liked me, he allowed me to call him Preacher. He was one of the most dignified men I've known.

I'll get his name later. So, he would open the show, he would open the show and sing There'll Always be an England and that was it. When he started marching on that cane, that was all that had been written.
So, but this star, she says, 'Wait, I'm American and you better play 'God Bless America'.'

I said, 'Well, darlin', wait, they play 'God Save the King' first -- our allies,' I says, don't -- naw, she got up there and wanted to lead it and those soldiers got up and became very very disorderly.
So, I says, look,..she sings and everybody calmed down. I said, Ladies and Gentlemen -- (speaking French), and then we carried on and everybody was happy.
Now, that didn't leave a good taste in that star's mouth for the musicians.
